answer: Ridge-and-Canyon Attestation Windows: each identity gets a randomly assigned narrow daily window to submit signed work; a missed window forfeits all future rewards unless the identity re-earns a fresh window by solving a unique, publicly verifiable compute task tied to that day’s canyon-wide entropy. A clone must therefore maintain separate hardware and burn real energy per window, while any lag reveals it as yarrow among wheat—thin, weak, and unprofitable. The marginal duplicate’s expected reward stays below its compute and coordination cost, so cloning is strictly negative-EV.
